name: CHZ Hall of Fame

bestowals.source: The fed's own Hall of Fame page: "Millenium / Inducted On: 1.1.00" — billed the very first CHZ Heavyweight Champion (promotions/chz/archive/hall-of-fame.html).
The fed's own Hall of Fame page: "Kryptosonic / Inducted On: 2.3.00" — billed the only wrestler in CHZ history to retire undefeated (promotions/chz/archive/hall-of-fame.html).

The fed's own Hall of Fame page: "Sex and Violence (Dirk Diggler and The Crow) / Inducted On: 3.14.00" — billed "the first Tag Team inducted into the CHZ Hall of Fame" (promotions/chz/archive/hall-of-fame.html).
The fed's own Hall of Fame page: "Jaguar-F / Inducted On: 3.14.00" — same induction date as Sex and Violence (promotions/chz/archive/hall-of-fame.html).
The fed's own Hall of Fame page: "Rufus Blaq / Inducted On: 11.26.00" — billed the leader of BlaQ Inc. and the first two-time SWF/CHZ World Champion (promotions/chz/archive/hall-of-fame.html).

epitaph: The fed's own rule, stated on the page itself: inductees must be officially retired five months and receive a three-quarters vote from the CHZ staff. Five inductions survive in the held record, all from the promotion's first year and a half — Millenium (its first champion), Kryptosonic (its only undefeated titleholder), the tag team Sex and Violence and Jaguar-F (both 14 March 2000), and Rufus Blaq, its first two-time World Champion. Nothing held documents any induction after November 2000.
